author: cnash03
text:
You don't have one. The $20/month Pro plan covers claude.ai and Claude Code, but not the API. API access is billed separately, pay-as-you-go.

**To get a key:**
1. Go to **platform.claude.com** (the Claude Console, formerly console.anthropic.com) and sign in. You can use the same email.
2. Under **Billing**, add a card and buy some prepaid credits. A few dollars is plenty for testing.
3. Under **API Keys**, click **Create Key** and copy it right away. It's only shown once.

**To use it in TaxWise:** `RagServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:45` reads `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from configuration. Locally, the simplest option is user-secrets, which keeps the key out of git:

```
! dotnet user-secrets set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY "sk-ant-..." --project src/TaxWise.Api
```

(If the project doesn't have a `UserSecretsId` yet, run `dotnet user-secrets init --project src/TaxWise.Api` first.) When you deploy to App Service, add it as an app setting with the same name.

**Watch costs while testing:** `appsettings.json` uses `claude-opus-5-5` with `MaxTokens: 16000`, which is the most expensive setup. While you iterate, you could switch to a Sonnet or Haiku model and set a spend limit in the Console under Billing → Limits.

prompt: is there another option can I just claude -p in my project insead of a api key

author: cnash03
text:
Technically yes: your .NET API could launch `claude -p "<prompt>"` as a child process and read what it prints. I'd recommend against it for TaxWise, though.

- **It breaks once you deploy.** `claude -p` runs on your Pro login on your Mac. App Service won't have the CLI installed or your login, so it only works on your machine.
- **It's against the terms.** A Pro subscription is for you personally using Claude and Claude Code. Using it to power an app that other people query isn't allowed, and for an app like that Anthropic expects an API key.
- **It's slower and gives you less control.** Every question starts a new CLI process, which adds seconds. You'd lose direct control over model, effort and max tokens, and you'd have to parse CLI output instead of SDK objects. It also uses up the same usage limits you code with.
- **You'd have to rework code that already exists.** `AskService` is built on the Anthropic SDK, so you'd be replacing working code with something more fragile.

Where it's reasonable: a one-off local script, like checking your prompts by hand during development. For the app itself, an API key is the right path. It's cheap if you buy $5 of credits, use a Sonnet or Haiku model while testing, and set a spend limit in the Console.

author: cnash03
text:
Yes. It would only work on a machine that has Claude Code installed and is logged in to a paid Claude account, and it would use that person's own usage limits.

That leads to a few problems:

- **Teammates and graders** couldn't run TaxWise unless each of them has a paid Claude plan and has run `claude` once to log in.
- **The deployed site** couldn't work at all, because no one is logged in on the App Service server.
- **Any user of the app** would be using the subscription of whoever's machine is running it, which is the part the terms don't allow.

With an API key, the key lives in config (user-secrets locally, an app setting on App Service), and the app works for anyone on any machine with no Claude account needed. That's why it's the standard approach. For a class project, $5 of credits with a cheaper model will probably last the whole semester.

author: cnash03
text:
The project already has user-secrets set up (`UserSecretsId` is `taxwise-dev`), so it's quick.

**1. Create the key**
1. Go to **platform.claude.com** and sign in.
2. Under **Billing**, add a card and buy credits ($5 is enough). The API won't accept calls until there's a balance.
3. Optionally, set a monthly spend limit under **Billing → Limits** (e.g. $10) so you can't get surprised.
4. Under **API Keys**, click **Create Key**, name it something like `taxwise-dev`, and copy it. It's only shown once.

**2. Save it locally.** Run this in the prompt here, pasting your key in:
```
! dotnet user-secrets set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY "[REDACTED]" --project src/TaxWise.Api
```
The key is stored in `~/.microsoft/usersecrets/taxwise-dev/secrets.json`, outside the repo, so it can't be committed. Each teammate does the same with their own key, or you share one privately (never in git or chat).

**3. Check it's saved**
```
! dotnet user-secrets list --project src/TaxWise.Api
```
Then run the API and hit the ask endpoint. You should get a real answer back instead of an auth error.

**4. When you deploy:** in the Azure Portal, open your App Service, go to **Settings → Environment variables**, and add `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` with the key as its value.

Once your key is saved, I can switch the model in `appsettings.json` to a cheaper one for testing if you want.

- Your `ant auth login` needs no code change. `ant auth status` shows you're logged in through the Mines organization. When no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set, the SDK uses that login automatically, and the app already allows for that. I updated two code comments to say so. The deployed site still needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` as an App Service setting.
- All 98 tests pass. The full build fails only in the MAUI app, because it wants Xcode 27.1 and you have 27.2. That's unrelated to this change.

It adds the four new decisions, the new things the AI got wrong (including that it only offered a paid key until you mentioned the university login), and a note that dev and production now use different models.

2. Development uses Sonnet 5.5 and production uses Opus 5.5.

`SETUP.md` should also tell your partner to run their own `ant auth login`. Your login is tied to your personal account, so it won't work for them.
